messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: High error rate and DNS timeouts observed for PrivateLink endpoints affecting customer peering across us-west-2 -> us-east-1 paths. Severity: P1. Pager to oncall-alex sent.

oncall-alex: ACK. Paging. Quick status — is this a control-plane DNS issue or data-plane packet loss?

network-eng-sam: I'm seeing BGP multipath churn between our peering fabric and customer edge in us-east-1. Route oscillation correlates with DNS failures due to TTL amplification at the provider edge (caches holding stale SRV/A records).

network-eng-sam: quick snippets: 
```
# traceroute from us-west2 proxy to privatelink-vpc-eu
traceroute to 10.10.30.1 (10.10.30.1), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.1.1  0.60 ms  0.54 ms  0.51 ms
 2  edge-usw2-ngx  2.3 ms  2.1 ms  2.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  edge-use1-agg  45.2 ms  44.9 ms  45.0 ms
 5  privatelink-eu-be  46.1 ms  46.0 ms  46.2 ms
```

network-eng-sam: And dig shows inconsistent answers from recursive caches in different regions: 
```
$ dig +short vpce-cust.private.example.com @8.8.8.8
10.10.30.1
# few minutes later
$ dig +short vpce-cust.private.example.com @8.8.8.8
10.10.99.5
```

network-eng-sam: So traffic flips between two backend prefixes, one of which is intermittently unreachable due to peering path suppression. Likely root cause: provider-side multipath hashing + transient BGP flap.

infra-sre-maya: Noted. Customer impact? Which customers/SLAs hit?

support-liz: We have 3 customers on dedicated PrivateLink connections showing 5xxs and connection resets: AcmeCorp, FinQuo, EduBase. Support tickets opened, customers notified about investigation. AcmeCorp reports failing webhooks and delayed requests since ~13:05 UTC.

oncall-alex: Ok. Triage plan: 1) remove the bad path from routing (temporary filter) 2) force DNS cache flush on our edge + request provider to flush upstream caches 3) enable fallback route (VPC peering) for impacted prefixes and shift traffic 4) keep customers updated. Sam/Maya take network steps, Liz draft comms.

network-eng-sam: Working on route filter now. Applying temporary BGP outbound policy to de-preference the problematic AS path (increase local-pref for primary). Command: 
```
bgp policy set AS_PATH 64500 deny-multipath
bgp local-pref set 200 for-prefix 10.10.30.0/24
```

network-eng-sam: Policy pushed to edge peering routers. Monitoring RIB and BGP table.

infra-sre-maya: I'll prep a DNS cache purge on our edge proxies. Triggering flush on edge nodes in us-west-2 and us-east-1. Command: `edge-proxyctl flush-cache --zone us-east-1 --names vpce-cust.private.example.com`

infra-sre-maya: Also raising a ticket with the transit provider to flush their recursive caches and to check for multipath hashing anomalies (ticket ID: TP-78321).

support-liz: Drafting message for customers: "We are investigating intermittent connectivity to PrivateLink endpoints; mitigation actions are underway. We'll update within 30 minutes." Want me to send now?

product-ops-ana: Please hold 10 minutes until we confirm route changes, then send an update with mitigation steps to avoid churn.

network-eng-sam: RIB now shows stable next-hop to primary prefix. BGP table no longer flapping for the impacted prefix. Watching data-plane pings to 10.10.30.1 — loss dropping from 35% -> 2% since policy.

infra-sre-maya: Edge cache flush completed in us-east-1 and us-west-2. Observed < 2s of elevated error rates during flush. Provider acknowledges cache flush request and started purge.

support-liz: Sent interim update to impacted customers (AcmeCorp/FinQuo/EduBase) with note: "We've implemented a temporary routing policy and flushed edge caches; please monitor. We'll follow up with RCA." Customers ack'd, AcmeCorp asked for ETA on full restoration.

oncall-alex: Good. Keep the temporary filter in place for now. Plan for full rollback after 2 hours of stability and post-incident RCA. Sam — collect BGP logs and timestamps for RCA. Maya — capture proxy cache metrics. Liz — gather customer impact windows and ticket numbers.

network-eng-sam: Collecting logs: `show bgp neighbors detailed | include 10.10.30.0/24` and exporting to S3: `bgp-export --prefix 10.10.30.0/24 --since 2365001000 > s3://redwood-incident-logs/2365001111/bgp.log`

infra-sre-maya: Storing cache metrics: `edge-monitor export --metric cache_ttl_hits --from 2365000800 --to 2365004000 > s3://redwood-incident-logs/2365001111/dns-cache.csv`

product-ops-ana: Are there any post-mitigation performance regressions? Latency/throughput change?

network-eng-sam: Slight latency bump (~10ms) due to forced path via primary region, but within SLA. No packet drops after changes.

support-liz: Customer confirmations: AcmeCorp — partial recovery (webhooks resumed); FinQuo — reports stable after 13:40 UTC; EduBase — still seeing some edge timeouts, but logs show retries succeeding.

noncall-alex: OK. We'll transition to monitoring mode. Handoff to infra-sre for follow-up and RCA. @network-eng-sam one more thing: leave the temporary filter in for 2 hours and then we can trial a controlled remove to ensure no re-flap.

network-eng-sam: Will do. Setting timer to re-evaluate at 15:00 UTC.

infra-sre-maya: I'll own the postmortem. Initial summary: root cause likely provider-side multipath BGP hashing combined with caching behavior at recursive DNS, leading to TTL amplification and stale A record responses during path oscillation. Mitigation: de-preference flaky AS path, flush caches, enable fallback peering for impacted prefixes. Next steps: coordinate with provider for long-term fix, consider more aggressive BGP dampening, and add synthetic PrivateLink probes in both regions.

support-liz: Tickets updated: ACME-4123, FINQ-8910, EDUB-7711. Will attach customer logs.

product-ops-ana: Thx. Please schedule a post-incident review with network, infra, and customer success in 48 hours.

noncall-alex: Closing pager. Monitoring continues. Great work. :thumbsup:
